# Conventions — idle-base

<!-- generated by /kb-generate — last_crawl_commit: bffd7f428878374fc80f9f2b7f802b85c6958dd2 -->

Everything below is observable in the code today. Where a rule has a canonical example, the
file path is cited — read that file before writing the equivalent.

## Code Style

- **CommonJS throughout**, including in `.js` files containing JSX: `const x = require('./x')`,
  `module.exports = { ... }`. No ESM, no TypeScript, no `import`. Babel handles JSX only.
- No semicolon-free style, no Prettier config in the repo; 2-space indent, single quotes,
  trailing commas in multi-line literals. Lines run to ~110 chars.
- **Comments explain WHY, at length.** This is the single most distinctive thing about the
  codebase. `src/data/acts.js` carries 40-line blocks recording simulation runs behind a tuning
  number; `src/engine/launch.js` opens with a fifteen-line argument for why it takes no `rng`;
  `src/engine/colony.js` records the measured freeze that `|| 0` instead of `Number.isFinite`
  would cause. Comments that restate the code are not the style — comments that record a
  decision, a measurement, or a bug that was fixed are. Match this or the change will look
  foreign.
- No linter is configured. There is no `.eslintrc`.

## Testing

- **There is no test runner.** `package.json` declares only `start` and `build`. No `jest`,
  no `vitest`, no test directory.
- The only automated gate is `npm run build` (webpack). It will not catch an
  undefined-dereference on a missing state slice, and it will not catch any of the three id
  lists in Act VII disagreeing.
- The conventional substitute: **drive the pure engines directly under `node`.** Everything in
  `src/engine/` and `src/data/` is plain CommonJS with no React import, so
  `node -e "require('./src/engine/colony')"` works without a build step. Tuning comments
  throughout `src/data/` cite results from exactly this (e.g. "30 runs per band", "measured:
  8 / 3s = 2.667 Salvage/s").
- For components, parsing under the repo's own Babel config is the available check.

## File / Module Organization

The three-way split is the architecture:

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| `src/data/` | Config and prose. **No logic.** Every tunable number and every player-facing string. |
| `src/engine/` | Pure logic. **No React, no DOM, no `Date.now()`, no bare `Math.random()`.** |
| `src/components/` | Render only. Decides nothing about rules, costs, odds or availability. |

Corollaries actually enforced in the code:

- A number inline in an engine or component is a bug. It belongs in a `*Config.js`.
- Player-facing prose lives in `src/data/` — see `feedMessages.js`, `toastMessages.js`,
  `storyBeats.js`, `propBetsConfig.js`, `actSevenPanels.js`. A string literal in a component is
  the same bug.
- Randomness enters an engine as a defaulted parameter (`rng = Math.random`) so behaviour can be
  driven headlessly with a deterministic generator. `engine/wallBall.js` and `engine/bookie.js`
  are the templates. `engine/launch.js` and `engine/puzzles.js` go further and take no `rng` at
  all — read launch.js's header for the argument, which is about offline catch-up resolving a
  dice roll in front of nobody.
- Components are one-per-file under a feature folder (`src/components/<feature>/`).
- Config files split by **reason to change**, not by convenience. `data/actSevenConfig.js` is
  the act's shape (read by engines and the save format); `data/actSevenPanels.js` is its surface
  (read by components). Nothing in `src/engine/` should need a tab label.

## Naming

- Files: `camelCase.js` for engines/data/actions/hooks; `PascalCase.js` for React components.
- Config files end in `Config.js` (`balanceConfig`, `actFourConfig`, `capsShopConfig`,
  `winPurseConfig`, `modifierKeysConfig`, `actSevenSitesConfig`, `colonyReadoutConfig`).
- Action types are `SCREAMING_SNAKE` string constants in `state/actionTypes.js`, value === key.
- Action modules are `<feature>Actions.js` exporting named `(state, action)` functions.
- Multipliers end in `Mult` (`revenueMult`, `strengthMult`, `gameSpeedMult`, `salvageOutputMult`,
  `lifeSupportDrawMult`) and are members of `BONUS_KEYS` in `data/modifierKeysConfig.js`.
  **A key not in that list is silently inert** — Act IV's `rookieQualityMult` shipped dead for
  exactly that reason. Act VII added six: `powerOutputMult`, `oxygenOutputMult`,
  `provisionsOutputMult`, `fuelOutputMult`, `salvageOutputMult`, `lifeSupportDrawMult`.
- Clock deadlines end in `AtClock` (`nextGameAtClock`, `nextChallengeAtClock`,
  `completesAtClock`, `nextClickAtClock`, `readyAtClock`, `arrivesAtClock`) and are compared
  against `state.clock`, which advances 1 per second.
- Feature ids in an act's `unlocks` array must equal the `PANELS` key in `AppShell.js` when they
  gate a whole tab. **Currency ids are not feature ids** — `acts.js` deliberately does not
  `unlock` `salvage`, because the header's chip filter would then start hiding caps and cash.
- Act VII offer ids are `<what>@<where>` — `colonize@onDeck`, `padTier3@firstBase`,
  `launch@secondBase`. The prefix *is* the stored `buildingId`, so `purchase()` writes what it
  parsed instead of translating through a mapping table. One vocabulary for the whole act.

## Notable Patterns

**Defaulting slice accessors — the most important pattern in the repo.** Saves are persisted to
`localStorage` and **never migrated** (`persistence/saveLoad.js` discards on version mismatch).
So every new state slice is read through an accessor that tolerates its total absence:

```js
function concessionsSlice(state) {
  const slice = (state && state.concessions) || {};
  return { stands: slice.stands || [], boosters: slice.boosters || [], /* … */ };
}
```

Canonical examples: `expeditionSlice()` in `engine/colony.js`, `wallBallSlice()` in
`engine/wallBall.js`, `concessionsSlice()` in `engine/concessions.js`, `capsShopSlice()` in
`engine/capsShop.js`, `bookieSlice` in `engine/bookie.js`, `getTeamName()` in
`engine/identity.js`. One `state.newThing.items.map(...)` white-screens an existing save on
load, and the build will not catch it.

Two corollaries the Act VII code adds:
- **A slice's base shape is written once and imported twice.** `createInitialState()` and the
  slice accessor must produce the identical shape; `data/actSevenConfig.js` holds the literal
  and both read it. A shop spreads the accessor's return value when it writes the slice back,
  so a key one copy forgets is a key every later write silently deletes.
- **`Number.isFinite`, not `|| default`, when 0 is a legitimate value.** Fuel's base capacity
  *is* 0. `||` cannot tell "not stored" from "stored as zero", and it also lets a non-number
  through — `('lots' || 0)` is `'lots'`, which becomes NaN in a rate, which becomes a NaN event
  clock, which permanently freezes `advance()`. `engine/colony.js`'s `normalizeResource()`
  documents the measurement.

**The shop contract.** Every shop engine exposes `listOffers(state)` returning presentation-ready
rows (`{ id, name, description, effect, cost, currency, owned, affordable, count, maxCount }`)
and `purchase(state, id)` returning new state or `null` for refused. The panel renders the rows
verbatim and recomputes nothing. See `engine/lotShop.js` ↔ `components/lot/LotShop.js` as the
reference pair; `concessions`, `wallBallShop`, `sponsorships`, `capsShop`, `actSevenModules`,
`sites`, `launch` and `puzzles` all follow it.

**Refusal is `null` from the engine, unchanged state from the reducer.** An action the player
could not have made through the UI is a no-op, not an error. Several call sites detect "nothing
happened" by reference equality, so return the *identical* object.

**Every wallet write goes through `engine/wallet.js`** (`creditWallet`, `debitWallet`,
`canAfford`, `balanceOf`). No currency may go below zero; this is structural, not a check.
**Act VII's four consumables are not currencies and must never be added to `data/currencies.js`** —
Power, Oxygen, Provisions and Fuel have capacity ceilings and signed net rates, live in
`state.expedition`, and are spent through `colony.js`'s `spendResource()` instead. Salvage *is*
an ordinary currency and is in the wallet.

**`EVENT_CLOCK_CONTRIBUTORS` is an append-only registration list** (`engine/tickEngine.js:230`).
A new wake boundary is appended; `findNextEventClock()` is never edited. The contract:
pure `(state) => clock | Infinity`, guard your **own** slice (every contributor runs in every
act, including acts where its slice doesn't exist), and return **`Infinity` — never 0, null or
undefined** — when nothing is pending. A contributor returning 0 pins the step at zero and burns
the whole 2000-iteration budget doing nothing; `Infinity` from all of them is what lets an 8h
offline return resolve in a handful of iterations. `engine/income.js` is the same shape for
income rates.

**Derived, never stored.** Unlocked features are recomputed from the act index (and, in Act VII,
the expedition phase) on every read (`getUnlockedFeatures`), so retuning an unlock takes effect
on an existing save with no migration. Crew size is *counted* from Respect rather than
incremented. `expedition.phase` is stored but **self-healing** — `sites.js:writeExpeditionPhase()`
recomputes it from a pure predicate ladder every iteration and is the only writer. Toasts are
derived from state transitions in `ToastHost.js` rather than pushed into state — its header
explains why: an 8-hour offline catch-up resolves a whole season inside one `advance()`, and a
stored-toast design fires a storm on load.

**Phase gating is a rank comparison, never equality.** `phaseRank()` in `data/actSevenConfig.js`
is the only way two phases should be compared: "has the run reached at least `lunar`", never "is
the run in `lunar`". An equality test is a rung that disappears from under a returning player.
The fail direction is deliberate and asymmetric: an **unrecognized phase fails open** (it is a
corrupt value one tick from self-repair, and failing closed could strand a save), while a
**missing site capability fails closed** (that is not corruption, it is the accurate statement
that the player hasn't colonized anything).

**Offline-catch-up safety is a design constraint, not an edge case.** `advance(state, deltaSeconds)`
runs live and on load with only `deltaSeconds` differing, and one iteration can span a whole
season. Anything that fires per-event must be idempotent and must not storm. The house idiom for
"announce once" is a persisted ledger diffed against the current set — `progression.storyBeatsSeen`,
`prestige.victoryAcknowledgedCount`, `sponsorBoard.announcedOfferIds`. Act VII's builds and
arrivals are idempotent by *construction* (a completed build clears its `buildingId`; a resolved
launch is never resolved again), and `expedition.puzzles` is never written from `advance()` at
all — the strongest form of the guarantee, and the one to copy where it's available.

**Two-axis act/era config.** `rules` *replace* a `balanceConfig` value (later layer wins, applied
by spread so a legitimate `0` differs from "absent"); `modifierBonuses` *accumulate* additively
into a clamped multiplier. `resolveRules(state)` and `computeModifiers(state)` in
`engine/modifiers.js` are the only readers. Never read `balanceConfig` directly for a value an act
or era can override — `StandingsPanel.js` resolving `playoffTeams` is the reference. Act VII adds
a third, intra-act layer: **`unlockedBy`** maps a feature id to the `expedition.phase` at which it
appears, holding back five of the act's six tabs after the act boundary has already unlocked them.

**`PRESTIGE_ACT_INDEX` (5) and `FINAL_ACT_INDEX` (6) are different numbers now.** They coincided
for the whole life of the repo until Act VII landed, and several call sites read
`FINAL_ACT_INDEX` and got the right answer by luck. Prestige returns the player to
`PRESTIGE_ACT_INDEX`; `FINAL_ACT_INDEX` means "the end of the authored arc" and is derived from
`ACTS.length`. `data/acts.js:466-491` and `engine/prestige.js:22` both document the trap — read
one of them before writing either constant.

**Bonuses apply at read time, never by mutating stored values.** `engine/strength.js` applies the
walk-up song multiplier inside `playerOverall` rather than writing to `player.stats`, so a stat
cap can't be laundered through a swap and the card can't disagree with the simulation. Same rule
in `engine/colony.js`: `resolvedSites()` merges site *definitions* over stored records, so
capability flags stay config and retuning them applies to existing saves.

**One solve, one helper.** `engine/colonyReadout.js` exists as a separate file so the header
can't derive its own rate: every field is arithmetic on one `colonyRates()` call. A header that
says 40 seconds while the engine crosses the boundary in 4 is worse than no warning at all.

**The manual click is never gated.** `engine/clicker.js` carries the anti-softlock guarantee: the
Hustle button exists in every act and always pays. A cooldown is a rate limit and acceptable; a
gate is not. Its currency and value are per-act overridable (`clickCurrency`, `clickFlatValue`,
`clickCooldownSeconds` in `acts.js`) — Act VII pays a flat 8 Salvage on a 3s cooldown, and since
every Act VII shop is Salvage-priced the button is the anti-softlock guarantee for that whole act.

## Mobile

The game is played on a phone; a 390×844 viewport is the target. `global.css` has a long
`Mobile` section documenting a header that had to be shrunk once already. Tap targets ≥44px,
nothing may scroll the page horizontally, and a `<select>` or text `<input>` needs
`font-size: 16px` or iOS zooms the page on focus. **`global.css` still ends inside its
`@media (max-width: 640px)` block** — appending a rule at EOF silently makes it mobile-only.
Feature-scoped section markers are the place to add rules; the Act VII sections (the header
resource readout, the teardown overlay) are placed deliberately *above* that final block and say
so in their headers.

## Visual identity

Act VII has its own palette and it is a rule, not a mood: the ballpark is warm and saturated
(green ground, gold, clay, outfield blue); Act VII is cold and near-monochrome with **exactly one
warm colour — the amber instrument glow.** Everything the player buys or reads is amber,
everything else is blue-grey. Tokens are `--v7-*` in `global.css`; the one runtime-read piece is
the per-phase pill in `data/actSevenPalette.js`, which mirrors `data/eras.js`'s `{ bg, ink }`
shape so `HeaderStats` renders both through one slot. Contrast ratios are **computed, not
eyeballed** — a 4.7:1 floor, with the arithmetic recorded at the foot of the file. Recompute if
a value moves.

## Git

- Feature branches named `story/<slug>` (28 of 31 merged PRs), with `feat/`, `fix/` and `chore/`
  used once each; PRs merged into `master`. 114 commits, 31 merged PRs at time of crawl
  (latest: #33).
- Commit subjects are sentences describing the change's *effect*, not conventional-commit
  prefixes — e.g. "Commit the burn: launch, transit, arrivals and the overshoot decision",
  "Wire act modifierBonuses into computeModifiers — Act IV was drafting adults".
- `openspec/` and `.claude/` are **tracked and committed** in this repo. A story that produces
  OpenSpec artifacts commits them alongside the code, usually in a separate commit ("Record the
  OpenSpec proposal, design, specs and tasks for …").
- Working tree is clean at time of crawl and `master` matches `origin/master`.
